newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Manila to try new scheme in battle against traffic.
newsitem.headline: Manila to try new scheme in battle against traffic.

text.p: Manila authorities struggling to cope with a worsening traffic situation in the city will try out a new scheme by reserving so called express lanes, officials said.
The express lanes will be reserved for the use of private cars which carry at least four passengers, Metropolitan Manila Development Authority (MMDA) traffic chief Romeo Maganto said.
"We are preparing the mechanics for such a scheme," Maganto told reporters.
He said the authority was considering reserving one lane along EDSA and Roxas Boulevard during an experimental period.
The MMDA had set aside special traffic lanes for five days until November 25 for the use of delegates coming to the Asia Pacific Economic Cooperation (APEC) forum.

Maganto said under the new scheme cars using express lanes would be exempt from existing restrictions which depending on number plates bars motorists from the streets one day each week. A date has not yet been set for the new scheme.

A local television station quoted Maganto as saying authorities would get around the problem of enforcing the minimum four passengers to a car rule for express lanes by banning cars using heavily tinted windows.
Dark tainted window glasses on cars so no one can see inside are common in Manila.
